ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, point A is on the curve $y_1=\frac{2}{x}$ ($x>0$), and point B is on the hyperbola $y_2=\frac{k}{x}$ ($x<0$), with AB parallel to the x-axis. Point C is a point on the x-axis, and lines AC and BC are connected. If the area of $\triangle ABC$ is 6, what is the value of $k$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Let the coordinates of point $A$ be $\left(a,\frac{2}{a}\right)$, then the coordinates of point $B$ are $\left(\frac{ak}{2},\frac{2}{a}\right)$\\
Thus, ${S}_{\triangle ABC}=\frac{1}{2}\times \left|a-\frac{ak}{2}\right|\times \frac{2}{a}=6$\\
We find $k=-10$, $k=14$ (discard)\\
Therefore, the answer is: $k=\boxed{-10}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there are coordinate axes, point A is located on the curve y=2/x in the first quadrant on the right side, and point B is located on a branch of a hyperbola in the second quadrant on the left side; line segment AB is horizontal. Point C is on the x-axis, and after connecting AC and BC, triangle ABC is formed. Since AB is horizontal, when the triangle takes AB as the base, the height is the distance from the common ordinate of A and B to the x-axis. Reasoning: Let A=(a,2/a), where a>0. Because AB is parallel to the x-axis, the ordinate of B is also 2/a. B is on y=k/x; let the abscissa of B be x_B, then k/x_B=2/a, solving gives x_B=ak/2, so B=(ak/2,2/a). From the figure and the meaning of the problem, B is on x<0, therefore ak/2<0; also a>0, so k<0. The area of the triangle is S=1/2·|a-ak/2|·(2/a)=6. Simplifying gives |1-k/2|=6. Thus 1-k/2=6 or 1-k/2=-6, solving gives k=-10 or k=14. Because it must have k<0, discard k=14, obtaining k=-10.
